title: PGE writes evaluatorFeedback and generatorNotes
description: Two of the three contract deltas exist because no PGE node writes these fields at all. Give the settled contract the same feedback and notes an imperative run records.

successCriteria.description: A settled contract from a graph run carries evaluatorFeedback with the same content an imperative run records for the same outcome.
Both are written from the node that owns the information, not copied from the seeded contract.
The contracts divergence is now down to `version` alone — asserted, not assumed.
Golden cases whose artifacts move are re-captured in this sprint, diff hunks read.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, and the golden gate passing at or above its replay floor.

nonGoals: Changing what the evaluator decides or what feedback it produces.
stopConditions: The graph engine genuinely lacks the information one of these fields needs — say which and why rather than writing a plausible-looking placeholder.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: The imperative writer is src/orchestrator/pipeline.ts around the settle site (it sets evaluatorFeedback from evaluation.summary). The graph equivalent settles at src/pge/nodes/sprint-review.ts:203-223. Write the fields there, from the same source of truth the imperative engine uses, so the two cannot drift by construction. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.
evaluatorNotes: Check the values MATCH rather than merely being present — a non-empty string that says something different is still a divergence. Confirm the source is the node's own evaluation result, not the seeded contract echoed back. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.
